_comment: The interpreter the desktop build ships. Pinned by hash, not by URL.
3.12 rather than 3.13: requires-python is >=3.12 and every wheel in
requirements.txt is pinned to a version tested there. The machine that
runs pip --target must be the same minor version — a mismatch installs
C extensions the shipped interpreter cannot load, and the error names
the module rather than the cause.
3.12.10 rather than a newer patch: CPython stopped publishing Windows
binaries for 3.12 when the branch went security-fix-only, so .10 is the
last release with an embeddable zip. 3.12.11 and 3.12.12 exist as source
How this sha256 was established: the archive was downloaded from the URL
below and its MD5 matched the MD5 python.org publishes for that file on
with the byte count matching the served Content-Length. The sha256 here
is that verified archive's. For a stronger chain, python.org also
Changing the version means redoing that check. The build refuses to run
with an empty sha256 rather than trusting a hash it computed itself.
